cobud

The goal of cobud is to make it easy to forecast Colorado’s General Fund budget. It includes historical budget data and example assumptions about future revenue, spending, and TABOR-related calculations. Custom assumptions can be supplied at varying levels of detail, from a single total appropriations figure to department-level detail, and can optionally draw on outside revenue and spending forecasts. Historical data, forecasts, and assumption templates are maintained by the Colorado Legislative Council Staff (LCS) economics team.

Installation

Instalation instructions are coming soon.

# example install

Example

To view historical budget data on Colorado’s General Fund, use the cobud_history data frame.

library(cobud)
library(dplyr)

# view historical budget data
cobud_history |> select(
  year,
  gf_start_balance,
  total_revenue,
  total_expenditures,
  gf_end_balance
)
#>     year gf_start_balance total_revenue total_expenditures gf_end_balance
#> 1  15-16               NA        9971.4            10189.7          512.7
#> 2  16-17            512.7       10275.8            10424.7          614.5
#> 3  17-18            614.5       11723.9            11215.4         1366.0
#> 4  18-19           1366.0       12564.6            12857.3         1262.6
#> 5  19-20           1262.6       12868.0            12778.9         1825.7
#> 6  20-21           1825.7       14310.1            13327.1         3181.5
#> 7  21-22           3181.5       17697.9            17838.7         3203.2
#> 8  22-23           3203.2       17998.0            19027.2         2427.4
#> 9  23-24           2427.4       17251.4            16870.8         3153.5
#> 10 24-25           3153.5       17181.3            18572.8         2408.4
#> 11 25-26           2408.4       16870.3            18062.7         2045.8

To forecast future years, load a parameter template, customize it, and feed that into cobud_forecast().

# load a parameter template
# and print the default assumption for inflation_pct
custom_params = very_simple_param_template
print(custom_params[["26-27"]][["inflation_pct"]])
#> $method
#> [1] "LCS forecast"
# edit that assumption
custom_params[["26-27"]][["inflation_pct"]] = list(
  method = "Custom", 
  value = 0.042
)

# run a forecast using default data and custom assumptions
custom_forecast = cobud_forecast(
  params = custom_params,
  historical_data = cobud_history,
  revenue_forecast = cobud_revenue_forecast,
  spending_forecast = cobud_spending_forecast
)
#> inputs validated
#> preparing tax credit triggers...
#>    for 25-26 ...
#>    for 26-27 ...
#> calculating 25-26 budget...
#>    using very simple appropriations...
#> calculating 26-27 budget...
#>    using very simple appropriations...
#> budget calculation successful
#> outputs validated
# preview the resulting forecast
custom_forecast |>
  select(
    year,
    gf_start_balance,
    total_revenue,
    total_expenditures,
    gf_end_balance
  ) |>
  tail()
#>     year gf_start_balance total_revenue total_expenditures gf_end_balance
#> 7  21-22         3181.500      17697.90           17838.70       3203.200
#> 8  22-23         3203.200      17998.00           19027.20       2427.400
#> 9  23-24         2427.400      17251.40           16870.80       3153.500
#> 10 24-25         3153.500      17181.30           18572.80       2408.400
#> 11 25-26         2408.400      16870.30           18062.70       2045.795
#> 12 26-27         2045.795      18038.48           18811.67       1327.014
